benchmark.ratio_interval_label: Conservative 95% sampling bounds from simultaneous Clopper-Pearson intervals. Excludes model uncertainty.

financial_basis.basis: incremental customer contribution or avoided cost, not vendor revenue

recommendation.title: Prioritize pulse optimization
recommendation.summary: Better gates increase simulated successful-shot throughput even after accounting for their longer duration. The price ceiling depends on the assumed application-value conversion and is a zero-NPV ceiling, not a recommended price or validated willingness to pay.
recommendation.price_ceiling_basis: maximum nonnegative total of equal annual installments; where gross value is positive it sets modeled customer NPV to zero. Zero may mean that no nonnegative fee can break even.
recommendation.initial_hypothesis: Prioritize AI calibration because eight hours of daily downtime appears to be the largest capacity opportunity.
validation_gates: Replay representative customer applications at matched wall-clock budgets, including reset, readout, leakage and drift.
Measure booked demand by time of day and identify which saved calibration windows could actually be sold or used.
Obtain an agreed dollar value for application outcomes before converting benchmark gains into a contract price.

assumptions.label: Daily calibration
assumptions.rationale: Nominal processor unavailability, before any overnight or demand adjustment.

assumptions.label: Observed bookings / available time
assumptions.rationale: Case observation. Default demand is 0.70 x (24 - 8) = 11.2 hours/day; the explicit demand field controls a scenario.

assumptions.label: Calibration tasks already automated
assumptions.rationale: The case reports a fraction of tasks, not a time share. Treating it as a time share is an explicit approximation.

assumptions.label: AI calibration speed claim
assumptions.rationale: The wording is 70% faster. It does not unambiguously mean 70% less time.

assumptions.label: Current two-qubit average gate infidelity
assumptions.rationale: Interpreted as full reported gate error in reported_total mode; mapping to an independent depolarizing channel is a modeling assumption.

assumptions.label: Proposed two-qubit average gate infidelity
assumptions.rationale: A proposed improvement in the fictional case, not independently measured evidence.

assumptions.label: Current two-qubit duration (ns)
assumptions.rationale: Disjoint two-qubit gates run in parallel within a layer.

assumptions.label: Pulse duration increase
assumptions.rationale: 420 ns at the case's 300 ns baseline.

assumptions.label: Median T1 (us)
assumptions.rationale: A median is not a device-wide distribution. Reported-total mode does not add this loss twice.

assumptions.label: Median T2 (us)
assumptions.rationale: Used for the alternate control-only noise interpretation, with T2 <= 2 T1.

assumptions.label: Representative workload qubits
assumptions.rationale: The device has 100 qubits; the representative workload uses 20. The benchmark does not simulate the whole processor.

assumptions.label: Entangling layers
assumptions.rationale: Even mirror-circuit depth; at 20 qubits this yields 200 two-qubit gates.

assumptions.label: Proposed total contract
assumptions.rationale: Assumed to include the selected product and, for controls, the supplied hardware. Do not add the hardware quote to this fee.

assumptions.label: Contract horizon (years)
assumptions.rationale: No terminal value, renewal, or residual hardware value is assumed.

assumptions.label: Conventional control procurement
assumptions.rationale: Only avoidable when an equivalent new procurement was already required. Installed purchase costs are sunk.

assumptions.label: Advertised hardware discount
assumptions.rationale: Standalone hardware quote is $1.4M at the case inputs, separate from the target total-contract analysis.

assumptions.label: Customer engineers for integration
assumptions.rationale: Customer cost; vendor engineering cost is not provided.

assumptions.label: Control integration (months)
assumptions.rationale: 3 engineers x 6/12 year x $300K = $450K.

assumptions.label: Customer cost per engineer-year
assumptions.rationale: No extra, unsupported engineering salary assumptions are added.

assumptions.label: Meaning of faster
assumptions.rationale: rate_increase uses time / 1.7, a 41.18% reduction; time_reduction tests the alternative 70% reduction reading.

assumptions.label: 10-to-100-qubit transfer
assumptions.rationale: Assumed fraction of pilot time-saving that survives full-device deployment. This is not a success probability.

assumptions.label: Freed time in usable windows
assumptions.rationale: Assumed fraction of saved calibration time reachable by customer demand. The case only says most calibration runs overnight.

assumptions.label: Daily demand scenario
assumptions.rationale: Fixed workload-hour demand; extra availability creates bookings only after the existing 16 hours are filled. No automatic demand growth is assumed.

assumptions.label: Reset, readout and host overhead per shot
assumptions.rationale: Illustrative fixed time per shot. It dilutes the relative penalty of longer entangling gates. Local Clifford-gate time is omitted.

assumptions.label: Value per baseline-equivalent productive hour
assumptions.rationale: Illustrative marginal contribution or avoided cost, not a known rental price or vendor revenue.

assumptions.label: Commercial value realization
assumptions.rationale: Fraction of the selected extra-output or fixed-output saved-time quantity that translates into monetizable application benefit. Explicitly unvalidated, not a probability or margin estimate.

assumptions.label: What creates financial value
assumptions.rationale: additional_output values B*(R-1), which needs demand for more useful output. fixed_output_savings values B*(1-1/R), the booked time avoided for the same benchmark output; only genuinely avoidable costs can be monetized. Calibration has no same-output speedup and earns zero capacity value in that mode.

assumptions.label: Operating days per year
assumptions.rationale: Assumed service calendar; maintenance and other fixed overhead are represented only to the extent captured by the case's booked time.

assumptions.label: Annual discount rate
assumptions.rationale: Illustrative time-value/risk hurdle. It does not validate the business or replace uncertainty analysis.

assumptions.label: Delay before recurring benefits
assumptions.rationale: Assumed deployment delay shared by capacity improvements. Fees remain payable at each year end; a delay beyond the horizon produces no recurring benefit.

assumptions.label: Equivalent new controls purchase required
assumptions.rationale: False means the existing $2M system is sunk. True credits avoidable $2M procurement. Integration cost is conservatively recognized at time zero.

assumptions.label: Noise interpretation
assumptions.rationale: reported_total uses reported full gate infidelities without adding in-gate T1/T2 loss again; control_only treats the reported errors as control errors and adds Pauli-twirled relaxation.

assumptions.label: Independent bit-readout error
assumptions.rationale: Not supplied in the case. Zero isolates the proposed two-qubit-gate improvement; it is not a claim of perfect hardware readout.

assumptions.label: Monte Carlo trajectories per circuit
assumptions.rationale: A computational budget. Binomial intervals reflect sampling error within this assumed model, not uncertainty about real hardware.

assumptions.label: Reproducibility seed
assumptions.rationale: Reproduce the circuit and simulated error trajectories using the exported scenario and software version.

warnings: All case inputs are fictional. The benchmark is simulated; no QPU, customer or vendor has validated these results.
Mirror-circuit success is a controlled benchmark, not application correctness. The dollar conversion requires customer validation.
The 35% already-automated task count is assumed to represent 35% of calibration time; a task-duration audit could change the result.
The 10-qubit AI pilot does not establish performance on the customer's 100-qubit processor.
The target contract includes the selected product. For controls it includes hardware, so the separate $1.4M hardware quote is not charged again.
Lower-cost controls are assumed to preserve current performance; that parity must be tested. Vendor delivery costs are unknown, so vendor profit is not estimated.
Baseline-equivalent productive hours can exceed wall-clock hours; they express benchmark throughput relative to the baseline.
Current demand fits inside existing availability. Faster calibration produces no additional booked hours in this fungible-demand model.
The installed $2M controls are treated as a sunk cost. A cheaper new control system does not create savings without a replacement need.
Reported gate error is interpreted as total average infidelity. Adding in-gate coherence decay again would double count it.
This scenario values additional useful output B*(R-1), not the smaller fixed-output saved-time quantity B*(1-1/R). Extra-output demand and willingness to pay must be established.
Mirror return is a benchmark proxy. A gain here does not establish customer application accuracy, billable demand, or quantum advantage.

assumptions.rationale: Assumed deployment delay shared by capacity improvements. Fees remain payable at each year end; a delay beyond the horizon produces no recurring benefit.

assumptions.label: Equivalent new controls purchase required
assumptions.rationale: False means the existing $2M system is sunk. True credits avoidable $2M procurement. Integration cost is conservatively recognized at time zero.

assumptions.label: Noise interpretation
assumptions.rationale: reported_total uses reported full gate infidelities without adding in-gate T1/T2 loss again; control_only treats the reported errors as control errors and adds Pauli-twirled relaxation.

assumptions.label: Independent bit-readout error
assumptions.rationale: Not supplied in the case. Zero isolates the proposed two-qubit-gate improvement; it is not a claim of perfect hardware readout.

assumptions.label: Monte Carlo trajectories per circuit
assumptions.rationale: A computational budget. Binomial intervals reflect sampling error within this assumed model, not uncertainty about real hardware.

assumptions.label: Reproducibility seed
assumptions.rationale: Reproduce the circuit and simulated error trajectories using the exported scenario and software version.

baseline.metric: all-zero return probability of the specified Clifford mirror
baseline.interval: 95% Wilson interval; shot noise conditional on this circuit
baseline.model: Pauli-frame Monte Carlo on a ring-connected Clifford mirror

pulse.metric: all-zero return probability of the specified Clifford mirror
pulse.interval: 95% Wilson interval; shot noise conditional on this circuit
pulse.model: Pauli-frame Monte Carlo on a ring-connected Clifford mirror

benchmark.ratio_interval_label: Conservative 95% sampling bounds from simultaneous Clopper-Pearson intervals. Excludes model uncertainty.
benchmark.duration_model: Parallel entangling layers plus explicit reset/readout/scheduling/local-gate overhead per shot.

financial_basis.basis: incremental customer contribution or avoided cost, not vendor revenue
financial_basis.value_quantity_definition: additional useful benchmark output expressed in baseline-equivalent productive hours
financial_basis.useful_hours_definition: annual mirror-benchmark capacity expressed in hours at the baseline successful-shot rate; not wall-clock hours or guaranteed application utility

recommendation.title: Prioritize pulse optimization
recommendation.summary: Better gates increase simulated successful-shot throughput even after accounting for their longer duration. The price ceiling depends on the assumed application-value conversion and is a zero-NPV ceiling, not a recommended price or validated willingness to pay.
recommendation.price_ceiling_basis: maximum nonnegative total of equal annual installments; where gross value is positive it sets modeled customer NPV to zero. Zero may mean that no nonnegative fee can break even.
recommendation.initial_hypothesis: Prioritize AI calibration because eight hours of daily downtime appears to be the largest capacity opportunity.
validation_gates: Replay representative customer applications at matched wall-clock budgets, including reset, readout, leakage and drift.
Measure booked demand by time of day and identify which saved calibration windows could actually be sold or used.
Obtain an agreed dollar value for application outcomes before converting benchmark gains into a contract price.

assumptions.label: Daily calibration
assumptions.rationale: Nominal processor unavailability, before any overnight or demand adjustment.

assumptions.label: Observed bookings / available time
assumptions.rationale: Case observation. Default demand is 0.70 x (24 - 8) = 11.2 hours/day; the explicit demand field controls a scenario.

assumptions.label: Calibration tasks already automated
assumptions.rationale: The case reports a fraction of tasks, not a time share. Treating it as a time share is an explicit approximation.

assumptions.label: AI calibration speed claim
assumptions.rationale: The wording is 70% faster. It does not unambiguously mean 70% less time.

assumptions.label: Current two-qubit average gate infidelity
assumptions.rationale: Interpreted as full reported gate error in reported_total mode; mapping to an independent depolarizing channel is a modeling assumption.

assumptions.label: Proposed two-qubit average gate infidelity
assumptions.rationale: A proposed improvement in the fictional case, not independently measured evidence.

assumptions.label: Current two-qubit duration (ns)
assumptions.rationale: Disjoint two-qubit gates run in parallel within a layer.

assumptions.label: Pulse duration increase
assumptions.rationale: 420 ns at the case's 300 ns baseline.

assumptions.label: Median T1 (us)
assumptions.rationale: A median is not a device-wide distribution. Reported-total mode does not add this loss twice.

assumptions.label: Median T2 (us)
assumptions.rationale: Used for the alternate control-only noise interpretation, with T2 <= 2 T1.

assumptions.label: Representative workload qubits
assumptions.rationale: The device has 100 qubits; the representative workload uses 20. The benchmark does not simulate the whole processor.

assumptions.label: Entangling layers
assumptions.rationale: Even mirror-circuit depth; at 20 qubits this yields 200 two-qubit gates.

assumptions.label: Proposed total contract
assumptions.rationale: Assumed to include the selected product and, for controls, the supplied hardware. Do not add the hardware quote to this fee.

assumptions.label: Contract horizon (years)
assumptions.rationale: No terminal value, renewal, or residual hardware value is assumed.

assumptions.label: Conventional control procurement
assumptions.rationale: Only avoidable when an equivalent new procurement was already required. Installed purchase costs are sunk.

assumptions.label: Advertised hardware discount
assumptions.rationale: Standalone hardware quote is $1.4M at the case inputs, separate from the target total-contract analysis.

assumptions.label: Customer engineers for integration
assumptions.rationale: Customer cost; vendor engineering cost is not provided.

assumptions.label: Control integration (months)
assumptions.rationale: 3 engineers x 6/12 year x $300K = $450K.

assumptions.label: Customer cost per engineer-year
assumptions.rationale: No extra, unsupported engineering salary assumptions are added.

assumptions.label: Meaning of faster
assumptions.rationale: rate_increase uses time / 1.7, a 41.18% reduction; time_reduction tests the alternative 70% reduction reading.

assumptions.label: 10-to-100-qubit transfer
assumptions.rationale: Assumed fraction of pilot time-saving that survives full-device deployment. This is not a success probability.

assumptions.label: Freed time in usable windows
assumptions.rationale: Assumed fraction of saved calibration time reachable by customer demand. The case only says most calibration runs overnight.

assumptions.label: Daily demand scenario
assumptions.rationale: Fixed workload-hour demand; extra availability creates bookings only after the existing 16 hours are filled. No automatic demand growth is assumed.

assumptions.label: Reset, readout and host overhead per shot
assumptions.rationale: Illustrative fixed time per shot. It dilutes the relative penalty of longer entangling gates. Local Clifford-gate time is omitted.

assumptions.label: Value per baseline-equivalent productive hour
assumptions.rationale: Illustrative marginal contribution or avoided cost, not a known rental price or vendor revenue.

assumptions.label: Commercial value realization
assumptions.rationale: Fraction of the selected extra-output or fixed-output saved-time quantity that translates into monetizable application benefit. Explicitly unvalidated, not a probability or margin estimate.

assumptions.label: What creates financial value
assumptions.rationale: additional_output values B*(R-1), which needs demand for more useful output. fixed_output_savings values B*(1-1/R), the booked time avoided for the same benchmark output; only genuinely avoidable costs can be monetized. Calibration has no same-output speedup and earns zero capacity value in that mode.

assumptions.label: Operating days per year
assumptions.rationale: Assumed service calendar; maintenance and other fixed overhead are represented only to the extent captured by the case's booked time.
